key_highlights: ASX faces heavy downside following Wall Street AI correction and a $169B weekly wipeout
Mounting recession warnings and RBA overtightening concerns weigh on investor sentiment
Household mortgage stress and accelerating Sydney housing price drops threaten bank credit growth
Department store restructuring highlights severe consumer discretionary weakness

sectors.trend: Mounting mortgage arrears and five rate hikes eroding borrowing capacity amid falling property values
sectors.implications: Net interest margins under pressure; higher loan impairment provisioning expected for major banks

sectors.implications: Multiple compression across high-PE growth names; capital raisings face heightened scrutiny

sectors.trend: Consumer spending contraction triggering deep retail restructuring and major headcount reductions
sectors.implications: Earnings downgrades likely across discretionary retailers; defensive discount operators to gain share

sectors.trend: Small-cap gold and rare earth exploration activity resilient despite broad macro headwinds
sectors.implications: Selective speculative interest in gold developers; diversified majors constrained by global demand outlook

sectors.trend: Regulatory friction regarding domestic gas reservation and energy security vs decarbonisation
sectors.implications: Policy uncertainty may cap capital expenditure while domestic supply shortages support local gas pricing

sectors.trend: Shifting dietary consumption patterns from GLP-1 weight-loss drugs altering grocery and pharma trends
sectors.implications: Potential structural volume headwind for packaged foods; defensive buffer in core healthcare services

sectors.trend: Ongoing work-from-home friction and residential property weakness impacting asset valuations
sectors.implications: Office and residential developers face cap-rate expansion and softened asset turnover

key_themes: RBA monetary policy overtightening and elevated domestic recession probability
Tech-led equity correction transmitting from US markets to the ASX
Severe household balance sheet strain dragging on credit and retail demand
Depreciating AUD impacting terms of trade and imported cost inflation

risk_assessment.mitigation: Increase allocations to defensive staples, sovereign bonds, and cash equivalents
Reduce exposure to unprofitable tech and high-multiple growth equities
Underweight banks with outsized exposure to highly leveraged residential mortgages
Hedge FX exposure; overweight unhedged offshore-earning ASX producers

opportunities.rationale: Gold serves as a safe-haven hedge against recession and currency debasement with strong project momentum

opportunities.recommendation: Selective Exposure to Low-Cost Energy Majors

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce High-Beta Tech and Discretionary Retail

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim Exposure to Major Retail Banks
defensive_moves.rationale: Surging mortgage stress, contracting borrowing power, and accelerated house price drops risk credit losses

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish over the next 1–3 months as the ASX digests Wall Street tech spillovers, weak retail data, and recession risks.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously neutral over 6–12 months, contingent on RBA rate cut pivot and stabilisation in domestic housing and commodity prices.
